note.text:
A figure has line symmetry (an axis of symmetry) if folding it along the line makes the two halves match. A square has 4 lines of symmetry, a rectangle 2, an equilateral triangle 3, a regular polygon with n sides n.
A figure has point symmetry (central symmetry) if a half turn (180°) about a point leaves it unchanged: parallelograms (and so rectangles, rhombuses, squares) and circles have it; triangles do not.
On a grid: the image of a point by reflection in the vertical line x = k is at the same height, the same distance on the other side: x′ = 2k − x.
By point symmetry about centre C, the image of M is M′ such that C is the midpoint of [MM′].

worked_example.problem: Find the image of A({x}, {y}) by reflection in the line x = {k}.
steps: A is {k - x} units to the left of the line.
Its image is {k - x} units to the right: x′ = {k} + {k - x} = {reflectX(x, k)}; y stays {y}.
worked_example.figure: coordPlane([['A', x, y], ['A′', reflectX(x, k), y]])

cards.idea: A line of symmetry folds the figure onto itself.
Point symmetry: a half turn about a point leaves the figure unchanged.
example: Every parallelogram has point symmetry about the meeting point of its diagonals.

cards.idea: Reflection in x = k: the image is the same distance on the other side.

check.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of the image of A({x}, {y}) by reflection in the line x = {k}.

misconceptions.explain: Reflecting in x = {k} is not just changing the sign (that is only for x = {0}).

solution: A is {abs(k - x)} units from the line.
Its image is {abs(k - x)} units on the other side: x′ = {answer}.

questions.prompt: How many lines of symmetry has {aOrAn(s)}?

misconceptions.explain: Check each line: the diagonals of a rectangle or parallelogram are not lines of symmetry.

solution: Fold the {s} in your mind along each possible line.

misconceptions.explain: {hasPointSym(s) ? 'Every parallelogram, and so this ' + s + ', looks the same after a half turn.' : 'After a half turn the ' + s + ' points the other way.'}

solution: Turn the {s} half a turn about its centre: {hasPointSym(s) ? 'it looks the same' : 'it does not look the same'}.

questions.prompt: M has coordinates ({x}, {y}). Find the coordinates of its image M′ by point symmetry about C({a}, {b}). Give the x-coordinate of M′.

misconceptions.explain: The centre is C, not the origin: x′ = {2} × {a} − {x}.
Go the whole distance again beyond C, not half.

solution: C is the midpoint of [MM′], so x′ = {2} × {a} − {x}.
